verdict.rationale: ObsessionDB documents OAuth 2.1 (rather than API keys) for connecting coding agents over MCP. It also documents role-based access scoped down to table and column, and running agents on isolated, read-only compute. Together these give agents a credentialed, least-privilege path. The docs do not explicitly show issuing a scoped credential to a specific agent or applying those roles to agent OAuth grants. missing for 10: explicit per-agent scoped credential or token issuance, documentation linking OAuth scopes or roles to agent sessions, revocation and expiry details for agent credentials, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Connect coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code, Zed) to your databases over MCP: OAuth 2.1, no API keys
Scope access with roles down to the table and column
an agent runs on isolated, read-only compute over the same data
